# Queue Management

`customer_support.support_operations.queue_management` · v1.0.0 · **draft**

**Is this queue absorbing what arrives, and who inside it is being forgotten?**


> Running the queue as a system with an arrival rate and a service rate, rather than as a list that someone works down. The competence is in three decisions: what order work is selected in, what is deliberately not being served while the queue is behind, and whether the gap between what arrives and what closes is being managed at the arrival side or only at the service side. It also owns the least popular thing in support operations — protecting the oldest end of the queue from a work-selection policy that will otherwise abandon it, because every incentive an agent has points at the newest, shortest, best-written ticket.

## Expertise applied


## Outcomes

- Arrival rate and service rate stated as one comparison, not as two dashboards that never meet.
- A published work-selection order that survives a busy shift — so selection is a policy the team can be held to, not a personal preference exercised under pressure.
- The oldest open item in every queue has a named owner and a stated reason it is still open.
- Deliberate degradation declared: when the queue is behind, what is being dropped, who decided, and who was told.
- The composition of arrivals attributed to a cause — a release, a campaign, a broken page, a genuine change in the customer base — rather than treated as weather.
- Queue state legible to someone arriving on shift who was not there when it went wrong.
- A standing distinction maintained between work that is paused on the customer and work that is paused on us.


## Failure modes

- Cherry-picking. Agents select the quick, well-written, easily-closed tickets. Handle time falls, closes-per-agent rises, average age improves, and the customers who have waited longest keep waiting. The queue reports its best week in the exact period it is failing worst the people it is failing.
- Measuring the backlog by count instead of by age. A shrinking pile of steadily older tickets reads as progress and is the opposite of it.
- Reading a queue near capacity as nearly fine. Wait time does not rise in proportion to utilisation — it rises far faster as arrivals approach the service rate — so a team described as almost fully busy is not a small adjustment away from comfortable, it is on the steep part of the curve where a single bad morning stops being recoverable.
- Staffing to the average. Support demand arrives in bursts; a team sized to the mean is drowning for part of every week and idle for the rest, and the drowning part is what the customer experiences.
- Reassignment as work. Tickets that move between queues accumulate handling without accumulating progress, and every hop resets somebody's sense of ownership while the customer's clock keeps running.
- Closing to clear. Bulk-closing aged tickets removes the symptom, keeps the demand, and returns as reopens and repeat contacts within the fortnight — now with a customer who has learned that waiting produces a closure notice.
- Parking in waiting-on-customer to protect the numbers. The state exists to pause a clock, not to hide work; a queue that leans on it rediscovers everything it hid, colder and angrier.
- One queue for work of wildly different service times. Short jobs wait behind long ones, no expectation can be set correctly for either, and the resulting average describes nobody.
- Managing to the mean. The mean hides the tail, and the tail is where the escalations, the churn signals and the executive emails are generated.
- Treating headcount as the only lever. Hiring moves the service side and moves it slowest; routing accuracy, deflection and product fixes move the arrival side and move it this week.
- Optimising a step that is not the constraint. Speeding up first-line when everything actually stops at a single specialist queue produces a faster route to the same wait.
- Owning a queue collectively. A queue with no named owner is not a queue, it is a place work goes to age.

## KPIs

| KPI | Unit | Direction | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| oldest_open_ticket_age | hours | lower_is_better | The single most diagnostic figure in a queue, because it is the one number cherry-picking cannot improve. |
| backlog_age_distribution | hours | lower_is_better | The shape of how long open work has waited, not its mean. The tail is the finding. |
| arrival_to_closure_ratio | ratio | target_band | Arrived over closed in the same window. Above parity the queue is growing whatever the headline count says today. |
| wait_before_first_touch | hours | lower_is_better | How long work sits untouched. Separates a slow queue from a slow resolution. |
| reassignment_rate | percent | lower_is_better | Share of tickets changing owner or queue. Rising values usually mean routing is failing upstream and the queue is paying for it. |
| reopen_rate | percent | lower_is_better | Read as queue pressure, not agent quality — it tends to track closure targets rather than skill. |
| touches_per_resolution | count | lower_is_better | Handling that produced no progress. The cost of unclear ownership and thin diagnosis. |
| peak_to_average_arrival_ratio | ratio | lower_is_better | Burstiness. The gap between this and parity is what a rota built on averages will fail by. |
| share_of_backlog_older_than_target | percent | lower_is_better | Deliberately expressed against a target held in the pack manifest rather than named here. |
| unassigned_queue_share | percent | lower_is_better | Work in the queue with no owner at all. Should be near-empty and is a leading indicator when it is not. |

## Metadata

owner **Customer Support** · updated 2026-08-08 · review **unreviewed** · confidence **provisional**


> No thresholds, no utilisation figures, no age bands. The utilisation curve is described by its shape because the shape is true of every queue ever run; the point on it where a given team starts drowning is arithmetic, differs between two queues in the same company, and belongs to Layer 4. A number in this file would mean the Layer 3/4 boundary had leaked. The load-set is honest about a harder problem: queue and backlog are planned objects that nothing in the shipped substrate emits, so almost nothing here can fire until a support pack ships derived.backlog_age and the ticket fact paths. That is the point of the backlog, not a caveat on this file.
